cars.generation: First-generation BC/BF Legacy production-road sporting family
cars.variant: RS E-BC5 five-speed manual — February 1989 Japan brochure reference
cars.specification_market: Japan February 1989 original Legacy RS E-BC5, standard five-speed manual. Actual original manufacturer RS brochure, hosted as scans by Play With LEGACY RS: printed pages 18–19 contain the model-specific specification table. EJ20-TURBO, horizontally opposed four-cylinder DOHC, 1994 cc, 92 × 75 mm, 8.5 compression, 220 PS at 6400 rpm and 27.5 kg·m at 4000 rpm. Native advertised units retained; no unstated SAE/net convention or PS/Nm conversion is introduced. Front and rear strut independent suspension and ventilated discs are explicit. No modified endurance-record-car or Group A specification, RA hand-built tune, GT automatic 200-PS engine, later twin-turbo calibration, optional equipment or competition result is imported as road performance. The photograph is a related 1990 RS Type RA road body, not authentication of this base 1989 reference.
cars.summary: The original turbo Legacy established Subaru’s EJ-powered AWD sports-saloon formula and underpinned its early World Rally Championship programme. The RS road car’s 220-PS boxer, manual transmission and performance chassis connect that engineering history to a production saloon. Count the first Legacy generation once across Legacy/Liberty and related badge identities, bodies and RS/GT/RA grades; years, equipment and competition derivatives add no extra counts.

cars.generation: Third-generation BE/BH Legacy / B4 production-road sporting family
cars.variant: S401 STI version GH-BES six-speed manual — 2002 Japan reference
cars.specification_market: Japan 2002 Legacy S401 STI version, GH-BES, six-speed manual; selected performance reference for the third-generation Legacy family. Actual live STI Japanese heritage page supplies 1994 cc, 92.0 × 75.0 mm, 9.0 compression, 216 kW (293 PS) net at 6400 rpm and 343 Nm net from 4400 to 5600 rpm. Native factory kW/Nm are retained without recalculating their rounded PS/kgf·m equivalents. STI confirms hand balancing, front LSD, 15:1 steering, Brembo brakes and reinforced suspension. Subaru’s model-specific November 2002 official catalogue supplies the flat-four DOHC 16-valve twin-turbo/EGI/AWD and suspension reference. Reference kerb/gross weights and the 240-km/h speedometer are not imported as certified mass or maximum speed. The announced 400-unit limit is not represented as an audited final production total. Standard RSK 280/260-PS manual/automatic, fourth-generation S402 and later naturally aspirated engines are not this car.
cars.summary: The S401 represents the third-generation Legacy’s STI-developed performance pinnacle: a hand-balanced turbo boxer, six-speed manual, front limited-slip differential and substantial steering, suspension and brake revisions. Those changes make it a distinct performance reference within the Legacy road lineage. Count the absent third generation once, including B4/Liberty, RSK/GT-B, sedan/wagon and S401 identities; the special edition does not create an extra count alongside its base family.
